items.headline: AI pricing tools are quietly shrinking Black Friday discounts at Gap, Under Armour and others
items.summary: Reuters, in a piece carried by BoF and FashionNetwork, reports that brands from Gap to Under Armour now use AI tools to set prices and decide when and how deeply to discount, and that the software often concludes promotions can be smaller without hurting demand. Examples from vendors include a beauty brand cutting a planned 40% Black Friday discount to 30% (Kapnova) and a buy-one-get-one offer trimmed from 50% to 40% (First Insight); Anaplan names Tiffany, Dolce & Gabbana and Saint Laurent as pricing clients. Centric Market Intelligence data show more sportswear on sale but shallower average markdowns, e.g. sports bras at 32% off versus 36% a year earlier.
items.why_it_matters: AI is moving from content to margin decisions in fashion; the same buyers approving AI pricing are the ones who will approve AI product imagery, and both pitches rest on measurable margin impact.

items.headline: Bangladesh garment wage talks stall as unrest costs an estimated $428M and moves orders abroad
items.summary: Sourcing Journal (WWD) reports that Bangladesh's minimum wage board failed to agree a new garment-worker wage on Monday after nine and a half hours of talks; an extended session follows on Tuesday. Workers' representatives want 32,000 taka ($257) a month, up from 12,500 taka, while owners call that untenable; the employers' undisclosed offer is said to exceed 14,500 taka. The BGMEA says buyers have moved confirmed orders for 59 million garments ($254M) to other countries, and a survey of 317 factories that halted work for 1-16 days this month puts losses at $428M FOB. Groups whose members include H&M, Gap, Primark, Levi's, Fast Retailing and Inditex have criticised the detention of union leaders.
items.why_it_matters: Sourcing shocks push brands to shorten sampling and shoot cycles; imagery that doesn't wait for physical samples helps absorb late or rerouted production.
items.notes: Article image shows protesters (identifiable people); not stored.

items.headline: Supreme and The North Face drop a skeleton-print 'Bones' collection on 27 November
items.summary: Supreme's first collection with The North Face in two years puts its Bones graphic on a 700-fill Nuptse puffer, a DryVent Mountain Jacket and matching pant, a pile fleece and a tee, plus a 34.5-litre rolltop backpack, balaclava and touchscreen gloves (Sneaker Bar Detroit). It releases on 27 November in Supreme stores and online. A preview post by @Ovrnundr passed 327,000 views on X within hours, and the campaign stars the Drain Gang collective.
items.why_it_matters: Hype drops sell out on product imagery alone; the Bones graphic wrapping a puffer is exactly the kind of print-placement detail on-model renders must keep exact.
items.notes: Image is the product shot of the Nuptse (via SupremeCommunity); the campaign image shows people and is not stored.

items.headline: Miu Miu names Thai-British actress Becky Armstrong brand ambassador
items.summary: Miu Miu announced on its official X account that Becky Armstrong, the Thai-British actress, is its new brand ambassador. The announcement video drew about 483,000 views and nearly 11,000 likes in 17 hours, and Vogue Thailand's post on the news collected over 2,600 reposts. It extends the Prada Group label's push with Thai talent, whose fan bases routinely drive the highest engagement on luxury posts in the region.
items.notes: Verified from the brand's official X account; no news article opened. No photo stored (real person).

items.headline: Vogue picks 'Heated Rivalry' star Connor Storrie for its 2026 Best Dressed cover
items.summary: Vogue named actor Connor Storrie, a Saint Laurent ambassador, its 2026 Best Dressed digital cover star, recapping a year that ran from a sharp-shouldered suit at the Golden Globes to a polka-dot halter top at the Met and PVC boots front row at Saint Laurent. In the Collier Schorr shoot, styled by Spencer Singer, he wears Loewe, Prada, Gucci, Versace, Loro Piana, Miu Miu, Calvin Klein Collection and The Row, often with Falke socks and Church's shoes. Pop Base's cover post passed 439,000 views on X, and several fan and film accounts drove another million-plus.

items.headline: Chiara Ferragni's Netflix documentary 'Chiara' lands and puts her back at the top of Italian X
items.summary: 'Chiara', the documentary in which the Italian influencer-entrepreneur tells her side of the past three years, began streaming on Netflix on 23 November (DonnaGlamour, citing SkyTG24). In a Vanity Fair interview tied to the launch she called the pandoro charity-sales operation a mistake for which she, as CEO, was responsible (Il Giorno). 'Ferragni' was among Italy's top X trends overnight, with one post about the film passing 283,000 views; reactions are split between sympathy and accusations of self-justification.

items.headline: NRF expects fewer Thanksgiving-weekend shoppers, but 59% plan to use AI to shop this season
items.summary: The National Retail Federation now expects 182.7 million people to shop over Thanksgiving weekend, down more than 2% on last year, as long pre-Black Friday sales pull spending forward (Retail Dive). Its survey of nearly 8,000 consumers found 59% plan to use AI to shop, mainly for product recommendations (32%) and gift ideas (31%), while 82% are reining in holiday budgets. Circana sees fourth-quarter holiday sales anywhere from -1% to +2.5% year over year.
items.why_it_matters: With most shoppers asking AI what to buy, product pages need imagery and data that assistants can parse and trust, not just human-facing banners.
items.notes: Article image is a stock photo of shoppers; not stored.

items.headline: Debenhams Group launches a Meta-powered AI Gift Finder inside WhatsApp
items.summary: Debenhams Group, which also runs boohoo, Karen Millen, PrettyLittleThing and Man, has launched a Gift Finder on WhatsApp built with Meta's AI (FashionNetwork). Shoppers arrive from Facebook and Instagram ads or a QR code, tell a business agent who they are buying for, their budget and preferences, and get recommendations plus a link to a pre-filled Debenhams basket. CEO Dan Finley frames it as in-store-style assistance on a platform customers already use.
items.why_it_matters: Conversational shopping shows a handful of products at thumbnail size in a chat; each SKU's lead image has to sell on its own.
items.notes: Campaign image shows models; not stored.

items.headline: Sizing-AI company MySize posts a 28% revenue drop and flags going-concern doubts
items.summary: Israel's MySize, which sells AI sizing software alongside fashion e-commerce and resale, reported third-quarter revenue down about 28% to $1.86M and a net loss of $1.80M, mainly on lower Amazon sales from thin inventory (Oui Speak Fashion). Its SaaS revenue grew 25% to $240,000 at roughly 82% gross margin and resale rose about 19%, but the company says current cash may not fund the next 12 months, raising substantial doubt about its ability to continue as a going concern.
items.why_it_matters: A reminder that fit-tech buyers will scrutinise vendor stability; standalone AI tools with small SaaS lines struggle when bundled with low-margin retail.
items.notes: Results released 20 Nov; article published 23 Nov. Article image shows models; not stored.

items.headline: Phoebe Philo opens a shop-in-shop at Dover Street Market Los Angeles
items.summary: Phoebe Philo opened a dedicated space at Dover Street Market's downtown LA store on Monday, carrying ready-to-wear, leather goods, shoes and accessories from Collection E plus earlier pieces; Collection F arrives in early 2027 (WWD). The fit-out uses brushed steel rails, cherry-wood vitrines and Douglas fir shelving. It joins her DSM shops in London, New York, Ginza and Singapore; Philo remains majority owner, with LVMH holding a minority stake.

items.headline: Rihanna's Lady Dior 2027 campaign is still one of the most-shared luxury images on X
items.summary: Rihanna fronts Dior's 2027 Lady Dior campaign, shot by Sam Rock under Jonathan Anderson's creative direction, in portraits alone and with her youngest child (Hypebae, 19 November). The imagery kept circulating over the weekend: a post pairing her with singer Tyla 'for Dior' passed 890,000 views on X, and campaign posts by fan accounts added hundreds of thousands more. She has also been the face of Dior's J'adore fragrance since 2024.
items.notes: Campaign verified (Hypebae); the X post's pairing of Tyla with Dior is an unverified social claim (no news source found). No photos stored (real people, includes a minor).

items.headline: Next says an online supplier was hacked but customer data appears safe
items.summary: UK retailer Next said on Monday that a third-party online supplier suffered a cyber incident giving attackers access to some data relating to the company, adding that current evidence shows no customer personal data was compromised and the information cannot be used for fraud (Reuters via FashionNetwork). It is the latest in a run of UK retail cyber incidents, after last year's attack that halted Marks & Spencer's online sales for about six weeks.

items.headline: The Interline: Straight Lines AI argues fashion needs AI image platforms, not one-off tools
items.summary: In The Interline's 'All About AI' series, Dale Kort of Straight Lines AI says fashion should no longer accept generative tools that 'just hallucinate sometimes' or that make teams sift many outputs to find one usable image. He pitches a platform layered over several foundation models with fashion-specific controls for colour accuracy, material rendering, construction details and consistency across a line, plus plugins, open APIs and integration with existing 3D pipelines.
items.why_it_matters: Same buyer objection On-Model faces daily: consistency and garment fidelity, not novelty, decide enterprise AI imagery deals.
